title: Kinesis Data Streams: shards, ordering and retention

videos.script: Every order Quitanda takes produces events. It is placed, packed, delivered, or cancelled. {{events}} Some programs need those events within seconds, not in tomorrow's export. A fraud check is one. The copy into the lake is another. That is what a stream is for. {{stream}} A Kinesis stream is not one long queue. It is a handful of shards, and each shard is its own ordered log. {{shards}} A record goes to one shard, chosen by the MD5 of a key you pick. You will predict that shard with a few lines of Python before writing anything. {{predict}} Then you will see what the order of events really means. It holds inside a shard, and nowhere else. {{order}} A shard also remembers for a fixed time and then forgets, and it can only take so much a second. {{limits}} Last, the money. A stream can be billed per shard or per gigabyte, and the same month costs three times as much one way as the other. {{price}}
